q: Was the sample deposited as GCA_026738955.1 actually the same physical isolate as the one MLST-typed as ST 492 in the paper, or did a sample mix-up occur between typing and submission?
basis: Independent pubMLST scan of the deposited assembly finds 5 exact allele matches (recA=1460, metG=124, gyrB=633, gltA=340, groL=91), zero of which match ST 492's expected profile (gyrB=112, groL=347, gltA=44, metG=217, ppsA=384, recA=381). Scan of all 2,756 pubMLST aeromonas profiles finds zero matching ≥3 of my alleles. This is not a within-species labeling drift - it's a complete profile-swap.
next_steps: Contact corresponding author (alimul.vmh@bau.edu.bd) with the deposited-vs-claimed allele table and request either (a) confirmation of which physical isolate matches which accession, or (b) resequencing of the ST 492-typed isolate. Also cross-reference the group's other WGS submissions to see if a systematic labeling issue exists.

q: How pervasive are cross-project accession errors in single-institution bacterial WGS papers, given the paper reports BioProject PRJNA810265 (which actually points to a Pasteurella multocida DC2020 project by the same institution) instead of the true PRJNA827572?
basis: One BioProject accession in the paper resolves to an entirely different organism submitted by the same lab. This is a copy-paste-shaped error. A bulk audit of NCBI-deposited genomes from Bangladesh Agricultural University's Department of Microbiology & Hygiene would establish base rate.
next_steps: Pull all NCBI-deposited genomes from submitter='Bangladesh Agricultural University' (currently ~50-100), cross-check reported BioProjects in the corresponding publications against the actual accession-organism mapping. Publish base-rate as a data-quality note.

q: For strains with phenotypic resistance to multiple antibiotic classes but no corresponding acquired mobile AMR genes at abricate default thresholds, how well does the PATRIC k-mer AMR pipeline's chromosomal-target + efflux-based prediction correlate with disk-diffusion phenotype?
basis: Paper reports phenotypic resistance to tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, streptomycin, neomycin. My abricate CARD scan finds only OXA-12, rsmA, cphA4 - all beta-lactam or regulatory. Zero acquired tet/qnr/aminoglycoside genes >=80% identity/coverage. If the paper's PATRIC AMR pipeline predicted 38 hits, the resistance mechanisms it uses (chromosomal SNPs, efflux) need phenotypic validation.
next_steps: Build a benchmark set of ~50 A. veronii genomes with paired disk-diffusion antibiograms, score sensitivity/specificity of PATRIC k-mer AMR predictions per antibiotic class vs abricate/AMRFinderPlus/hAMRonization. Focus especially on efflux-only genotype predictions.

q: When multiple close comparator genomes sit within ~0.3% ANI of a query strain (Alim_AV_1000 vs TH0426=96.34%, B565=96.34%, FDAARGOS_632=96.47% - all essentially indistinguishable by ANI), what phylogenetic-inference method reliably resolves 'closest relative' and how does the answer change with reference-set composition?
basis: Paper concludes closest to TH0426 + B56 via RaxML tree on PGFam-aligned proteins. ANI does not distinguish these three references. The claim is topological, not distance-based, and topology can be sensitive to which of ~1,262 A. veronii genomes are included.
next_steps: Rerun the paper's phylogeny with 3 different reference-set expansions (all fish-A.veronii, all 1,262 A.veronii, matched-year comparator set) and report tree-topology stability at the 'closest sibling' branch. Publish a 'closest-relative fragility index' for A. veronii clade.

q: The deposited contig-level assembly (93 contigs) shows one contig with 16 phage-family genes and 6 additional contigs with 3-gene fragments each - if the same DNA were resequenced with Nanopore/PacBio and hybrid-assembled to closure, how many of the fragmented prophage regions would coalesce into intact prophage loci, and would that reclassify the paper's '2 intact + 1 incomplete' count upward?
basis: Assembly is short-read only (Illumina + MEGAHIT), coverage 186x, but 93 contigs indicates repeat-driven fragmentation. Prophage regions are notoriously repeat-rich (attL/attR, tail-fiber diversity). Two contigs carry strong prophage signal (78: 16 genes, 90: 7 genes) but many 3-gene fragments could plausibly belong to a single fragmented larger prophage.
next_steps: Retrieve the isolate (or a fresh Bangladesh Shing-fish A. veronii from BAU repository), do R10.4.1 Nanopore + Illumina hybrid, assemble to closure with unicycler/trycycler, then rerun PHASTER. Also useful: PHASTEST on the current assembly with the 'fragmented prophage detection' mode explicitly turned on to compare against the paper's PHASTER default.
